summary: VulnGym aligns 184 reviewed GitHub high-severity advisories (Nov 2025-Apr 2026, repos >10k stars) with vulnerable repository snapshots and annotates 408 entries with line-level entry points (EP), critical operations (CO) and EP-to-CO traces. It defines one end-to-end detection task (agent gets repo plus advisory title/description) and three oracle-conditioned subtasks, and evaluates Qwen3.5 2B-27B under Claude Code plus three open-weight frontier LLMs under Claude Code, OpenHands and MiniSWE with read-only shell tools. All configurations score low, especially on the Hard subset.

claims.claim: Current coding agents remain limited in end-to-end repository-level vulnerability detection.
claims.evidence: Table 2: best Hard-subset T1 result is OpenHands+DeepSeek-V4-Flash at 22.58% AR / 15.22% ER / 11.63% ES; Qwen3.5-27B under Claude Code 12.90% AR. But Hard is only 31 advisories / 46 entries, so 22.58% = 7/31 advisories; one run per configuration, no CIs.
claims.location: §Frontier Coding Agents on Hard Cases, Table 2

claims.claim: Scaffold-LLM compatibility is critical; scaffolds differ in sensitivity to LLM choice.
claims.evidence: Table 2: DeepSeek-V4-Flash 22.58% AR with OpenHands vs 9.68% with Claude Code; GLM-5.2 reverses (6.45% vs 12.90%); MiniSWE identical 16.13% AR for all three LLMs. Differences are 1-5 advisories out of 31 in a single run, so reversals may be noise.

claims.claim: EP identification is harder than CO localization; traces stay incomplete and noisy even with oracle endpoints.
claims.evidence: Table 3: max CO FR 51.16% / LR 30.23% vs EP FR 30.23% / LR 18.60%; TNR 30.60-53.96% vs TNP 14.61-26.71%; max ES 36.37%. Consistent across 9 configs, but on 43 Hard items only.

claims.claim: Higher resource consumption does not necessarily yield more effective detection.
claims.evidence: Figure 7 token/cost vs AR scatter over 9 configs; OpenHands+GLM-5.2 highest cost, lowest AR. Only 9 points, no statistical test.

claims.claim: Benchmark annotations are reliable (two independent reviewers, Cohen's kappa 0.87, senior adjudication).
claims.evidence: Phase II text reports kappa=0.87; however Phase I record 'generation' method is not described (unclear whether LLM-generated), and the difficulty split counts 110/31/31 advisories and 278/56/46 entries (172/380) do not sum to the headline 184/408 without explanation.

patterns.note: Agents restricted to read-only grep/rg/find/cat; trajectory analysis (Fig. 6) shows search and read dominate, yet line-level localization still fails in 56.5% of Hard failures (wrong file or wrong line).
New repository-level security benchmark with oracle-conditioned subtasks for diagnosis.
Reports tokens and USD per run vs accuracy (Fig. 7); no budget mechanism tested.
No execution or PoV validation at all; agents could not run code, which limits what the low scores say about agents with verifier loops.

methodology.sample: 184 advisories / 408 entries across 23 repos; headline agent comparison on Hard subset of 31 advisories / 46 entries (T1) and ~43 items in oracle tasks (inferred from percentages).
methodology.baselines: No non-agent baseline (e.g., SAST tool or function-level LLM classifier); comparison is among 3 scaffolds x 3 LLMs and a Qwen scaling series. No Claude/GPT models despite using Claude Code.
methodology.variance: None; single run per configuration, no seeds or CIs.
methodology.ablations: Oracle-conditioned subtasks act as a capability decomposition; no prompt/tool ablations.
methodology.contamination_controls: Advisories restricted to Nov 2025-Apr 2026 as 'after training cutoff'; per-model cutoffs not verified. T1 supplies the advisory title and description, which strongly hints at location.
methodology.languages: Not stated; Fig. 2 shows repository composition (e.g., Open WebUI). Language mix of the 23 repos not reported.

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint, no venue in comment or journal_ref.
standards.artifacts: No benchmark or code link found in the text; only third-party URLs (OpenHands, Open WebUI, an advisory).

biases.detail: Headline frontier comparison uses 31 Hard advisories; each 3.2-point step equals one advisory.
Single run per configuration; scaffold-LLM 'reversals' are within plausible run-to-run noise.
Benchmark claimed as contribution but no dataset/code release link in the paper.
T1 'detection' gives the advisory description, so it measures localization of a known vulnerability, not discovery; k=5 line window can also penalize semantically correct alternative traces.
Training cutoffs of evaluated models are asserted not verified; advisory text supplied in prompt.
Claude Code is run with non-Anthropic open models; no Claude/GPT backends, so 'frontier coding agents' is overstated.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Claude Code, OpenHands, MiniSWE scaffolds; DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Qwen models. None from Tencent.
coi.funding: No acknowledgments or funding statement found.
coi.detail: Tencent security-team authors build a benchmark; no Tencent product is ranked. Vendor affiliation only.

verdict_reason: Useful diagnostic decomposition (EP vs CO vs trace) with decent annotation agreement, but headline comparisons rest on 31 advisories, a single run, open-weight models only, no artifact link, no limitations section, and unexplained count mismatches.
applicability: Indirect. For the Java backend team it argues against relying on a read-only coding agent as the security review gate across several repositories: even with the advisory text supplied, agents mislocate entry points (API handlers/event callbacks — exactly the service endpoints) and produce noisy cross-module traces. Better to keep SAST (Semgrep/Sonar) as the deterministic gate and use agents to triage findings. The scaffold-model sensitivity result, though weak, is a caution for mixed agent hosts: do not assume a model's quality transfers between Claude Code, OpenHands and others. Language mix is unreported, so Java-specific transfer is unknown; CWE-Bench-Java/JavaVulBench are closer fits.

conflicts_with.detail: Revelio reports agentic detection finding 19 new memory-safety bugs by gating on executable PoV + sanitizer; VulnGym's pessimism comes from read-only agents without execution, so the two disagree on how capable agentic detection is because of the verifier setup.
